historical_record.description: Recorded in the city's survey of the Van Ness Avenue automobile corridor as built for use as an auto showroom. Dated 1920–1921. Designed by Weeks and Day for the Cadillac dealership of Don Lee. It was monumental in scale and luxurious in detail, and pulled the centre of the showroom trade several blocks south.
Cadillac dealerships occupied the building into the 1960s. Its integrity survived its conversion into a cinema.
Evaluated in the city's survey of the Van Ness Avenue automobile corridor and given California Register status code 3CS — individually eligible for the California Register, under Criteria 1, 2 and 3.

Two hundred demonstrators organised by the local NAACP chapter picketed the Don Lee Cadillac dealership here on 14 March 1964, part of the Auto Row employment campaign; 107 were arrested. Seven of the dealership's 258 employees were Black.
